name: MinuteCryptic
description: Can an LLM solve real Minute Cryptic daily clues (definition + wordplay) from minutecryptic.com, and how does its hint usage compare to human par?

binding_vow.description: One real Minute Cryptic daily clue per episode. Every observation carries the rules of cryptic crosswords and a common-substitutions cheat sheet. The first observation gives only the clue and the answer's length. Each turn the agent either GUESSES the answer or replies 'HINT'. Wrong guesses are non-terminal and are listed back to the agent; the same wrong answer three times ends the episode. 'HINT' walks an escalating, persistent ladder: the official progressive hints first (definition -> wordplay -> ...), then the answer's letters revealed one at a time in the official order, which guarantees the episode terminates. Scoring is golf-style against the clue's par (expected number of hints). Reward is paid once, on the terminal step.

observation_space.description: { "clue": string, "enumeration": string e.g. "(7)" or "(3,4)", "answer_length": int, "word_lengths": [int], "rules": string, "common_substitutions": [string], "hints_taken": int, "par": int, "instructions": string, "revealed_hints"?: [string], "revealed_letters"?: string (e.g. "S _ E _ _ _ _", '/' marks a word break), "wrong_guesses"?: [string], "feedback"?: string }

action_space.description: Free text: either the agent's answer, or exactly 'HINT' to reveal the next hint (official hints first, then one answer letter at a time).

reward.description: Terminal-step reward: 1.0 correct with no hints; max(0.2, 1.0 - 0.2*hints) correct after hints (the same formula whether the hints were explanatory or letter reveals); 0.3*similarity when the same wrong answer is guessed three times; 0.0 if truncated without answering.
